title: HVZ Reaction and Why Benzoic Acid Goes Meta
subject: Chemistry
objective: Two places a carboxylic acid can be substituted: the α-carbon (HVZ: X₂ and red phosphorus, then water) and the benzene ring of an aromatic acid, where –COOH is deactivating and meta-directing and blocks Friedel-Crafts reactions.

fill.q: In the HVZ reaction the halogen is used with a small amount of red ____.
CH₃COOH gives ____ acid in the HVZ reaction with Cl₂.
–COOH on a benzene ring is a ____-directing group.
Nitration of benzoic acid gives ____-nitrobenzoic acid.

tf.q: HVZ replaces an α-hydrogen by a halogen.
tf.explain: The product is an α-halo acid.

tf.q: Benzoic acid undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation easily.
tf.explain: The ring is deactivated and AlCl₃ bonds to –COOH.

ar.a: Benzoic acid is nitrated at the meta position.
ar.r: –COOH withdraws electrons and leaves positive charge at ortho and para.

ar.a: Trimethylacetic acid does not give the HVZ reaction.

mcq.q: The HVZ product from propanoic acid with Br₂ / red P, then water, is:
mcq.explain: The bromine goes to the α-carbon (C-2).

mcq.q: In benzoic acid, positive charge from resonance appears at:

num.q: How many α-hydrogens does acetic acid have?
steps: The CH₃ carbon is the α-carbon.

short.q: Give two reasons why benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction.
short.solution: The ring is deactivated by –COOH; the catalyst AlCl₃ (a Lewis acid) bonds to the carboxyl group.
